question.:question/worked-solution:
We use the quotient rule with the numerator $u(x)=(5x+4)^{2}$ and the denominator $v(x)=x.$ 

Differentiating $u(x)$ and $v(x),$ we have

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=10(5x+4),\,{v}^{′}(x)=1.
$$

Note that we used the chain rule to differentiate $u.$

Now, applying the quotient rule and simplifying, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\ & =\frac{10(5x+4)x-(5x+4)^{2}}{x^{2}} \\ & =\frac{(5x+4)(5x-4)}{x^{2}} \\ & =\frac{25{x}^{2}-16}{x^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
